message.content:
**Source:** S0014, student trajectory, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r1/fixed_h/H0/fixed_version_test/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to JSONL lines in that file; supplied observations are complete line ranges, not split excerpts.

| Stage | Evidence and distinction |
|---|---|
| Goal | The instruction requested a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, including camera, framing, materials and occlusions, without using the reference as a background or texture (student request, line 1). The student’s “Victorian bedroom” is its interpretation, not independent evidence of the unseen photograph (student response, line 3). |
| First build | The program specified multiple objects: room, windows, bed, chair, screen, table and rugs. It positioned separate bed rails, posts and pillows, rotated pillows, and specified a camera, emitters and procedural materials (student response and execute, lines 3–4). These operations do not verify part connections, pose or visual match. Step 1 failed at `world.use_nodes` because the world was `None`; no image was returned (execution result, line 5). |
| Repair and validation | The student received the traceback in the next request (line 6), then added a conditional world creation and made smaller portrait and miniature changes (student response, line 8; execute, line 9). Step 2 reported success, saved a render and blend file, and was selected (execution result, line 10; select, line 11). The log reports 16 render samples despite the program requesting 48. A successful render is technical validation, not visual or geometric verification. |
| Review and unexecuted revision | Reference and step-2 render were supplied to the student for comparison, with zero executions remaining (student request and session, lines 12–13). The student then returned another complete program: it rotated the bed and chair, changed the room and door, camera lens, lighting and material-selection logic, and added a triangular cloth mesh (student response, line 14). No execution or selection of that revision is recorded. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or receipt is present in this student trace. The traceback was runner feedback, not teacher advice; the subsequent world fix is visibly consistent with that feedback. The student independently authored and revised programs; the three recorded sessions report no tool calls (lines 2, 7, 13). No separate exploration beyond these responses and runner executions is visible.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Step 1 was a technical failure; step 2 was a successful build/render and selection. Overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not formal visual success or proven algorithm failure. The final response was a nonempty but unexecuted revision, not an empty patch. Neither image is visible in the supplied observations: object presence in the reference, actual texture appearance, connectedness, pose, framing, illumination and render defects cannot be independently assessed. The code’s name-based material assignment may or may not have affected intended meshes; the later dimension-based approach is only an untested hypothesis.

**Lessons.** Transferably, runtime errors and image fidelity require separate checks: fixing the world initialization enabled rendering but did not establish a match. Task-specific camera, orientation and material revisions remain hypotheses because the execution budget was exhausted (lines 10–14).
